requirements.text: TEST PROBE 2

Deliver a single consolidated end-to-end systemic audit report covering architecture, database, backend, contracts, frontend, security, distributed systems, integrations, dependencies/supply-chain, test strategy, documentation accuracy, reliability/observability, performance, UI/UX, accessibility, adversarial/residual findings, and git/repo integrity for MUSIC OS 360.
nonRequirements: No fixes, refactors, migrations, or code edits are implemented or committed as part of this mission; deliverable is analysis plus a proposed, NOT-executed implementation plan. The pre-existing uncommitted naming-normalization diff (per git status at mission start) and its already-landed PT->EN rename commits are read-only context and must not be staged, unstaged, committed, reset, or otherwise modified by this mission.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Final report contains one consolidated document including: coverage ledger, architecture/domain map, source-of-truth map, writer/reader matrix for material entities, producer/consumer/contract map, canonical naming findings classified by type, findings by severity with file:line evidence, security findings, residual-audit results, AI-skills/agent-pack capability map, and a prioritized implementation plan.
git status --short and git diff captured at end of mission are identical to the snapshot captured at mission start (no files staged/unstaged/committed/reset by this mission's activity).
The report contains zero applied code diffs; the plan section is explicitly labeled NOT EXECUTED / PENDING AUTHORIZATION.

requirements.text: Audit the in-progress PT->EN naming normalization (titulo/title, tipo/type, data_inicio/data_fim->start_date/end_date, obra_id->work_id, documentos->documents, client/project/campaign/release FK families) for completeness and consistency across DB, backend, and frontend.
nonRequirements: This mission does not perform additional renames or edits; it only verifies claims already recorded in NAMING_NORMALIZATION_CANONICAL_MAP.md against current code/DB state and reports gaps.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every canonical rename pair listed in NAMING_NORMALIZATION_CANONICAL_MAP.md is checked by repo-wide search against apps/api/src, apps/web/src, and migrations/entities, and classified as fully-migrated, partially-migrated (with file:line holdouts listed), or not-migrated.
Report includes a source-of-truth map naming, per renamed concept, which layer (DB column, TypeORM entity, DTO, frontend type) is authoritative and which are stale/duplicated definitions.
Every residual PT-named field, column, or variable still referenced in live (non-test, non-comment) code is reported with file path and line number.

requirements.text: Produce an architecture and domain map of MUSIC OS 360 covering every module in apps/api/src/modules and apps/web/src/modules, plus packages/*.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report includes a module/domain map covering every top-level directory under apps/api/src/modules, apps/web/src/modules, and packages/*, each with stated responsibility and its known dependents.
Coverage ledger lists every module/directory that was audited versus explicitly skipped-with-reason; no module is silently omitted from the ledger.

requirements.text: Audit database schema and multi-tenant isolation guarantees across all tenant-scoped entities in apps/api.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every entity/table with a tenant-scoped column is classified as DB-enforced (FK/RLS/unique-with-tenant constraint) or application-only enforced, with file:line/migration evidence for the classification.

Every TypeORM repository or query-builder call found not scoped by tenant id is listed by file:line, or the report states explicitly that a repo-wide search found none and describes the search method used.

Migration history is diffed against current entity definitions for at least the tables touched by the in-progress naming normalization, reporting any drift between committed migrations and entity code.

requirements.text: Audit API/DTO contracts between apps/api controllers and apps/web TanStack Query consumers for drift.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A producer/consumer/contract map is produced for every REST endpoint exposed by apps/api, comparing the NestJS DTO/response shape against the actual frontend call/type shape, flagging every field-name or type mismatch with file:line on both sides.
Every contract mismatch found is classified by severity (breaking / silent-fallback / cosmetic).

requirements.text: Audit distributed-systems correctness of BullMQ queues/processors in apps/api: idempotency, retries, and failure handling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every BullMQ queue/processor is inventoried with its idempotency mechanism (or none found), retry/backoff configuration, and dead-letter/failure handling, each with file:line evidence.
Every job handler performing a mutating operation without an identifiable idempotency guard is reported as a finding with an assigned severity.

requirements.text: Audit external platform integrations (Spotify, Soundcharts, and any other providers under apps/api/src/modules/artists/platform-profiles/providers and elsewhere) for auth, rate-limiting, and error handling.
nonRequirements: Verification is read-only; no live external API calls requiring write credentials are made during the audit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every external provider integration is inventoried with its auth method, rate-limit handling, and error/retry handling, each with file:line evidence.

The currently unresolved-merge-conflict and staged files in the platform-profiles module (artist-external-profile-sync.service.ts, spotify-artist-profile.provider.ts/.spec.ts, ArtistaPlatformMetrics.tsx and its test, per git status at mission start) are reviewed and their conflicted/staged state is documented in the report without being resolved.

requirements.text: Audit dependency and supply-chain risk across apps/api, apps/web, and packages/* (vulnerable, unpinned, or abandoned packages).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report lists results of a dependency vulnerability check (e.g. pnpm audit or lockfile inspection) across apps/api, apps/web, and packages/*, enumerating every high/critical advisory by package and version.
Any direct dependency found with no pinned/ranged version, or with an abandoned/unmaintained status discovered during the audit, is flagged as a finding.

requirements.text: Audit test coverage posture across backend and frontend modules based on actual presence of spec/test files, and flag DI-wired services with no tests.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report states, per backend and frontend module directory, whether matching spec/test files exist, derived from actual file search rather than assumption.
Every backend service class that is imported into a NestJS module's providers array (i.e., wired into DI) with no corresponding spec file is flagged as a finding.

requirements.text: Re-verify every major claim in AUDITORIA_COMPLETA_MUSIC_OS_360.md, AUDITORIA_DOMINIO_E_ARQUITETURA.md, AUDITORIA_SISTEMICA_TOTAL.md, and MUSIC_OS_360_FORENSIC_AUDIT.md against current code, treating them as claims rather than ground truth.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every major claim/finding in each of the four prior audit documents is classified as still-valid, stale/already-fixed, or contradicted-by-current-code, with file:line evidence supporting the re-verification.
Any finding from a prior audit document that this mission cannot reproduce is explicitly listed as not-reproduced rather than silently dropped from the report.

requirements.text: Audit reliability and observability instrumentation (logging, error tracking, health checks, metrics) across apps/api.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report inventories logging, error-tracking, health-check, and metrics instrumentation present in apps/api, and flags any critical path (auth, tenant isolation, and billing/payment if present) with no logging or alerting on failure, with file:line evidence.

requirements.text: Audit apps/api and apps/web for performance anti-patterns: N+1 queries, missing indexes on tenant-filtered columns, and unbounded/unpaginated queries.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every N+1 query pattern, missing index on a frequently tenant-filtered column, or unbounded query lacking pagination/limit found via code inspection is reported with file:line evidence.

requirements.text: Audit apps/web for UI/UX and accessibility issues: missing alt text, missing form labels, missing keyboard focus handling, and hardcoded low-contrast colors.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report inventories apps/web pages/components for missing alt text, missing form labels/aria attributes, missing keyboard focus handling, and hardcoded color values relevant to contrast, each finding class supported by file:line evidence.

requirements.text: Audit git/repo integrity: document the current uncommitted/staged/conflicted state of the working tree exactly as found, without resolving it.
nonRequirements: This audit does not resolve the unresolved merge conflicts (UU files) or the staged/uncommitted naming-normalization diff; it only documents their state.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report documents the exact git status (staged/unstaged/untracked/conflicted files) captured verbatim at mission start as a fixed reference snapshot.
Every file listed with UU (unresolved merge conflict) status in that snapshot is opened and its conflict-marker state (or resolved-but-uncommitted state) is documented by file path in the report.

requirements.text: Audit application-level security: authentication/authorization guard coverage on all API routes, and presence of hardcoded secrets/credentials in the repo.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every controller route in apps/api is checked for an auth guard; any route with no guard and no explicit public-route justification is reported with file:line evidence.

Report lists results of a repo-wide secret scan (hardcoded API keys/passwords/tokens in source, config, or committed .env-like files) with every hit listed by file:line, or states explicitly that none were found and the search method used.

requirements.text: Map the .claude/ agent/skill pack's own architecture (agents, skills, runtime scripts, rules) as a dedicated workstream of this audit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report includes a capability map of every agent, skill, rule, and runtime script under .claude/, listing what each is triggered by and what actions/writes it is permitted to perform.
Any skill/agent whose declared write/permission scope is inconsistent with its stated purpose (e.g., a read-only investigation agent configured with file-write permission) is flagged as a finding.

requirements.text: Classify every finding in the report by severity and category with evidence, and run a dedicated adversarial/residual pass for race conditions, missing authz, committed secrets, and spoofable tenant IDs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every finding in the final report has an assigned severity (critical/high/medium/low), a category, and either file:line evidence or an explicit statement that it cannot be pinpointed to a line, with a description in its place.

The residual/adversarial pass explicitly reports present-or-absent status for at least: race conditions on concurrent writes, missing authorization checks on admin-only endpoints, secrets committed to git history, and tenant-id values spoofable from client input.

requirements.text: Produce a prioritized implementation plan addressing this audit's findings, explicitly not executed in this mission.
nonRequirements: No item in the plan is implemented in this mission; every plan item requires separate, later authorization before work begins.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every plan item links back to at least one finding ID from this report; there are no orphan plan items without an underlying finding.
Every plan item is ordered/tagged by priority derived from finding severity and explicitly labeled NOT YET AUTHORIZED / NOT EXECUTED.

findings.summary: clientIp() trusts X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP/CF-Connecting-IP headers verbatim with no Express trust-proxy validation (no app.set('trust proxy', ...) in create-app.ts) and no allowlist of known proxy hops. Rate-limit identifier is IP:route, so an attacker can set an arbitrary X-Forwarded-For (or X-Real-IP) value per request to get a fresh bucket every time, fully bypassing RateLimitGuard including the 5-req/15min 'auth' category that is the only brute-force protection on /auth/* login/password endpoints.

RateLimitService uses an in-process Map (sliding window held in memory) with no Redis/shared backing despite REDIS_QUEUE_URL being mandatory in production and multi-instance deployment being the norm; comment at top of file explicitly flags this as a stopgap ('Para producao com Redis: substituir'). Under horizontal scaling each instance enforces its own independent 5-req/15min auth limit, so effective brute-force protection scales up with instance count instead of staying fixed.

Infinite recursion / stack overflow when a payment_grace or read_only tenant crosses the suspend threshold: getState() -> applyOverrideAndEscalation() -> suspendTenant() -> getState() (nested) -> applyOverrideAndEscalation() -> suspendTenant() ... recurses forever because suspendTenant's own 'before = await this.getState(tenantId)' re-reads the still-unmodified DB row (its own UPDATE runs later in the function) and getState() re-evaluates the same expired-suspendAt condition, calling suspendTenant again before the first call ever reaches its UPDATE statement.
findings.rootCause: suspendTenant() fetches its audit 'before' snapshot via the public getState() (which itself triggers escalation as a side effect) instead of a raw, non-escalating SELECT of the current row; there is no re-entrancy guard between applyOverrideAndEscalation and suspendTenant, so any code path that calls suspendTenant from inside escalation (the normal payment_grace/read_only -> suspended transition, and also removeManualOverride when the override was masking an already-expired grace window) recurses unboundedly and the tenant can never actually be persisted as suspended.

findings.summary: getState() is a query with a disguised command/side effect: it calls applyOverrideAndEscalation() internally, which performs a real UPDATE (read_only or suspended transition, or removeManualOverride) as a side effect of what every caller (BillingEnforcementGuard, DunningService, and getState()'s own recursive self-calls) treats as a cheap read invoked on every authenticated HTTP request. This is genuine CQS-violation debt, worsened (not created) by P0-A: the guard now calls this write-capable getState() on every single guarded request instead of only reading the boolean tenants.active column TenantGuard used before.
findings.rootCause: No separation between the pure state read and the escalation/transition command; the transition logic was folded into the getter for reuse between the guard and the scheduler instead of being invoked explicitly by both callers alongside a plain, non-escalating read.

findings.summary: enqueueNotification's dedup-key comment ('tenant_billing_state.updated_at only changes when applyOverrideAndEscalation actually moves the tenant to a new status') is factually inaccurate and understates how often the dedup key changes: suspendTenant() and startPaymentGrace() both unconditionally set updated_at = now() on their ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE branch even when the tenant is already in that status (idempotent re-entry, e.g. two Stripe webhook retries, or the concurrent-recursion scenario in the sibling finding), and billing.service.ts's updateAdminTenant writes tenant_billing_state directly. Each such no-op write produces a new dunning-notify jobId and therefore a new duplicate notification, independent of the previously-confirmed staleness issue.
findings.rootCause: The dedup key assumes updated_at is a proxy for 'semantic status changed', but every UPSERT in billing-enforcement.service.ts bumps updated_at unconditionally rather than only on an actual status transition (e.g. via a WHERE status IS DISTINCT FROM ... guard or a dedicated status_changed_at column).

findings.summary: Additional legacy readers of tenants.active beyond the ones already catalogued (TenantGuard, docusign, external-data): apps/api/src/modules/leads/leads.service.ts:326 (public lead-capture/registration lookup, unauthenticated) and apps/api/src/modules/integrations/autentique/autentique.service.ts:77-85 (Autentique e-signature webhook, @Public()) both still gate purely on tenants.active. Since nothing in the automated billing path sets tenants.active=false anymore (the core regression already confirmed), these two additional, previously unlisted checks are also permanently neutered for any tenant suspended only through tenant_billing_state — widening the already-confirmed blast radius beyond the 2 webhooks named in the review brief.
findings.rootCause: tenants.active was the shared, single boolean multiple independent modules (guard + 2 webhooks + leads public form + Autentique webhook) relied on as ground truth for tenant enforcement; P0-A stopped writing it from the automated dunning path without auditing or migrating any of its readers to tenant_billing_state, so every one of these reader sites silently degrades to 'always active' for suspensions reached exclusively via the new canonical table.
